question: Can the strongest bounded channel-neutral six-scale scene-linear diffusion family suggested by ProMist-5K explain an additive exposure-domain backing-return observation across unseen exposures and structures, or does nonlinear response make the two mechanisms identifiable?

primary_source.title: ProMist-5K: A Comprehensive Dataset for Digital Emulation of Cinematic Pro-Mist Filter Effects
required_text_anchors: six Gaussian blur layers with progressively larger kernels
blurred layers are combined with the original
primary_source.reproduction_boundary: The paper does not publish exact kernel radii or blend weights. P3S tests a clean-room equation family constrained by the published topology, not the authors' unreleased renderer or dataset targets.

controls.single_scale: the same fitted family restricted to sigma=8 pixels
controls.correct_topology: the exact frozen additive backing-return truth equation

branch_rule.all_gates_pass: Treat channel-neutral post-lens diffusion as observationally equivalent under this synthetic protocol; real halation acquisition must add wavelength, layer, backing or geometry evidence before mechanism claims.
branch_rule.any_gate_fail: Retain a multi-exposure mechanism discriminator and require exposure bracketing in future real halation evidence; do not tune scales, response, split, weights or gates on this cohort.

forbidden_actions: claim that ProMist-5K measures photographic-film halation
claim exact reproduction of unpublished ProMist-5K kernel radii or weights
use generated or learned final RGB
change scales, response, roles, objective or gates after the formal score
promote a stock, physical calibration or product renderer from synthetic evidence
claim_ceiling: synthetic identifiability evidence separating a latest published scene-linear lens-diffusion equation family from additive pre-development film backing return; no real-film, stock, calibration, visual-quality or product claim
